metadata.name: Visual Genome
metadata.description: A dataset of over 100,000 images with dense annotations designed to connect language and vision for cognitive tasks. Each image contains an average of 21 objects, 18 attributes, and 18 pairwise relationships, which are structured into scene graphs. The dataset also includes an average of 42 region descriptions and 17 question-answer pairs per image. All objects, attributes, relationships, and noun phrases are canonicalized to WordNet synsets.
metadata.citeAs: Ranjay Krishna, Yuke Zhu, Oliver Groth, Justin Johnson, Kenji Hata, Joshua Kravitz, Stephanie Chen, Yannis Kalantidis, Li-Jia Li, David A. Shamma, Michael S. Bemstein, Li Fei-Fei. Visual Genome: Connecting Language and Vision Using Crowdsourced Dense Image Annotations. arXiv:1602.07332v1 [cs.CV] 23 Feb 2016.

rai:responsibleAIMetadata.rai:dataCollection: The dataset uses 108,249 images from the intersection of the YFCC100M and MS-COCO datasets. All annotations, including region descriptions, objects, attributes, relationships, and question-answer pairs, were collected and verified entirely by crowd workers on Amazon Mechanical Turk. The collection process involved a multi-stage pipeline to first gather natural language descriptions of image regions, and then extract structured data (objects, attributes, relationships) from these descriptions to build scene graphs.
rai:responsibleAIMetadata.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The dataset was collected over the course of 6 months, following a 15-month period of experimentation and iteration on the data representation.
rai:responsibleAIMetadata.rai:annotatorDemographics: A total of over 33,000 unique workers contributed. 93.02% of workers were from the United States. The majority of workers were between 25 and 34 years old (ages ranged from 18 to 68). There was a near-balanced gender split of 54.15% male and 45.85% female workers.
rai:responsibleAIMetadata.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for training and benchmarking computer models for comprehensive scene understanding. Specific applications mentioned include modeling object relationships, image description, visual question answering (VQA), semantic image retrieval, robotic interactions, dense image captioning, and relationship extraction.

metadata.name: FLORES-101
metadata.description: The FLORES-101 evaluation benchmark consists of 3001 sentences extracted from English Wikipedia and professionally translated into 101 languages. The dataset covers a variety of topics and domains and is multilingually aligned, enabling the assessment of many-to-many multilingual translation systems, particularly for low-resource languages.
metadata.license: Source text is from Wikimedia sources, available under permissive licensing.
metadata.citeAs: Goyal, N., Gao, C., Chaudhary, V., Chen, P. J., Wenzek, G., Ju, D., ... & Guzmány, F. (2021). The FLORES-101 Evaluation Benchmark for Low-Resource and Multilingual Machine Translation. arXiv preprint arXiv:2106.03193.

rai:responsibleAIMetadata.rai:dataCollection: Source sentences were extracted from English Wikimedia sources: one-third from Wikinews, one-third from Wikijunior, and one-third from WikiVoyage. For each source article, 3 to 5 contiguous sentences were manually selected. These sentences were then translated into 101 languages by professional translators through a carefully controlled process involving multiple Language Service Providers (LSPs) for translation, editing, and quality assurance.
rai:responsibleAIMetadata.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The paper does not specify start and end dates for data collection. However, it notes that the translation and re-translation process for a single language took on average 61 days, with the longest turnaround being 89 days.
rai:responsibleAIMetadata.rai:annotatorDemographics: The initial English sentences were selected by 10 annotators from the research lab (6 male, 4 female) from diverse regions. The translations were performed by 'professional translators' and evaluated by 'human evaluators' via Language Service Providers (LSPs). No further demographics about the translators are provided.
rai:responsibleAIMetadata.rai:dataUseCases: The primary use case is the evaluation of low-resource and multilingual machine translation, especially many-to-many systems. Other supported tasks include document-level translation, multimodal machine translation (using associated metadata like images), multilingual text classification, sentence and document classification, language identification, and multilingual domain adaptation.
rai:responsibleAIMetadata.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The paper does not mention any specific procedures for handling personal or sensitive information. The data is sourced from public Wikimedia projects (Wikinews, Wikijunior, WikiVoyage) covering general topics.
